title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: A control algorithm has zero value on a whiteboard; its worth is measured when it cranks a wet-magneto scooter silently in 45°C Delhi traffic or synchronizes a backup genset in 10 seconds flat.
epigraph.author: Operating lens on embedded mechatronics

web_blocks.html: SEDEMAC reports operations across two primary segments: Mobility and Industrial [4]. In FY26, Mobility generated ₹912 Cr (86.2% of ₹1,058 Cr total revenue), up from ₹564 Cr (85.7%) in FY25 [4]. Industrial contributed ₹146 Cr (13.8%), up from ₹94 Cr (14.3%) in FY25 [4]. Beneath these two segments sit four distinct product families. These are (1) Sensorless ISG ECUs and combined ISG+EFI controllers (~60–64%+ of revenue), (2) standalone EFI and Aftertreatment Control Modules (ACMs), (3) EV Motor Control Units (MCUs) and traction motors, and (4) Industrial Genset AMF and engine EFI controllers [7, 8, 9, 13].

web_blocks.title: Concrete Example 1 — Mobility ICE: Wet-Magneto Sensorless ISG + EFI on a Mass-Market 2W
paragraphs: Customer & Problem: TVS Motor needed BS-VI compliance, silent starting, and idle start-stop on high-volume platforms like Jupiter, Ntorq, and XL100 [7, 15]. Conventional starter motors added weight, gear noise, and mechanical wear. Placing Hall-effect sensors inside hot, oil-immersed magnetos also posed reliability risks [7].

SEDEMAC Product & Integration: SEDEMAC supplies a combined ISG + EFI ECU powered by patented Sensorless Commutation (SLC) software (US12015315B2 / US12119769B2) [7, 10, 11]. At low RPM, the ECU injects current pulses and reads intra-PWM ripples in the stator windings [11]. This infers exact rotor position without physical sensors. It cranks the engine silently, then switches to battery-charging alternator mode and manages fuel injection [7, 15]. Sold under multi-year OEM contracts, this single-box design lowers system BOM and assembly complexity [7].

web_blocks.title: Concrete Example 2 — Mobility EV: ISAAC Motor Control Unit & Logan Traction Systems
paragraphs: Customer & Problem: Indian electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler OEMs suffer field failures when water, dust, or heat degrades Hall-effect sensors inside traction motors [9]. They also face supply-chain exposure to Chinese rare-earth magnets [9].

SEDEMAC Product & Integration: SEDEMAC supplies its ISAAC sensorless Motor Control Units (MCUs) and Logan rare-earth-free motor platforms [9]. Running sensorless control in firmware eliminates the fragile motor-side sensor harness and cuts connector failures [9]. EV MCUs scaled from 0.3% of mobility sales in FY24 to meaningful commercial volumes in FY26–H1 FY27, hedging long-term ICE-to-EV substitution [1, 5].

web_blocks.title: Concrete Example 3 — Industrial: GC500/GC800 AMF & CPCB IV+ EFI for Backup Gensets
paragraphs: Customer & Problem: Hospitals, offices, and telecom sites running diesel or gas generators (from Kirloskar, Mahindra Powerol, or Generac) need fast grid-failure detection and sub-10-second cranking [8, 13]. They also require true-RMS phase protection and strict CPCB IV+ emission compliance up to 8 cylinders [8].

SEDEMAC Product & Integration: SEDEMAC supplies panel-mounted GC500/GC800 AMF controllers alongside engine-mounted, IP67-rated EFI ECUs and electronic governors [8]. The AMF unit monitors utility voltage, commands transfer switching, and logs fault telemetry. Meanwhile, the EFI ECU meters air-fuel ratios in real time to meet CPCB IV+ limits [8]. In FY26, this industrial vertical grew 55% YoY from ₹94 Cr to ₹146 Cr [4, 8].

web_blocks.html: A clear strategic thread links all three examples. SEDEMAC is extending its sensorless control stack into cordless power tools and smart FET voltage regulators [5, 9]. It is also preparing wet-magneto ISG kits and export 3-wheeler ISG ECUs for H2 FY27 and FY28 rollouts [5]. Still, investors must weigh the current revenue reality. ISG-led ICE two-wheeler electronics generate most cash flow today, while EV MCUs and new OEM programs are still ramping [1, 13].

book_paragraphs: To see SEDEMAC clearly, strip away the buzzwords like 'deep-tech' and 'mechatronics' and look at the actual boxes rolling off its assembly lines in Pune. Every rupee of SEDEMAC's ₹1,058 crore FY26 revenue comes from two reporting segments: Mobility at ₹912 crore (86.2% of sales) and Industrial at ₹146 crore (13.8% of sales). Both segments rest on the exact same engineering foundation—embedded software that senses what a rotating machine is doing without needing fragile physical sensors bolted onto the shaft.
Let us walk through three concrete, real-world examples so you can picture how each segment works in the field.

Start with Mobility ICE, which is still the beating heart of the company—ISG and combined ISG+EFI controllers alone account for roughly 60% to 64% or more of total revenue. Picture an engineer at TVS Motor designing a mass-market scooter like the Jupiter or Ntorq, or a commuter workhorse like the XL100. When India mandated BS-VI emissions and OBD Stage II-B diagnostics, carburetors had to go, and riders increasingly expected silent, button-press starting plus idle start-stop at traffic lights. A conventional starter motor whirs loudly, chews up gears, and adds weight. Putting Hall-effect position sensors inside a wet, oil-splashed magneto invites warranty claims. SEDEMAC solves both headaches in one box: its combined ISG+EFI ECU uses patented Sensorless Commutation algorithms to pulse tiny currents into the stator windings, read the electrical ripples, and calculate the exact rotor angle in microseconds. It cranks the engine silently, then flips seamlessly into alternator mode to charge the battery, while simultaneously metering fuel injection. For the OEM, one SEDEMAC box replaces a starter motor, a clutch mechanism, position sensors, and a separate EFI computer.

Now shift to Mobility EV, SEDEMAC's bridge to an electrified future. Electric scooters and e-rickshaws suffer from a notorious field headache: water ingress during monsoons or thermal stress kills the Hall-effect sensors inside traction motors, stranding riders. SEDEMAC's ISAAC series Motor Control Units apply the same sensorless firmware to electric traction motors, while its Logan motor platform explores rare-earth-free designs that reduce dependence on Chinese permanent magnets. EV revenue was just 0.3% of mobility in FY24, but commercial shipments ramped meaningfully through FY26 and H1 FY27 as OEMs qualified the units for production.

Finally, look at the Industrial segment, which grew 55% in FY26 from ₹94 crore to ₹146 crore. Walk into the basement of an Indian hospital or a commercial office park and open the control panel of a Kirloskar or Mahindra Powerol backup generator—or look at small-engine gas gensets in North America built by Generac. Inside that panel sits a SEDEMAC GC500 or GC800 Automatic Mains Failure controller, commanding roughly 75% of the Indian AMF market. The moment grid power drops, the controller verifies phase voltage, cranks the engine, transfers the load in seconds, and logs telemetry. Alongside it, under India's stricter CPCB IV+ emission norms, SEDEMAC supplies rugged, IP67-rated engine-mounted EFI controllers for diesel and gas gensets up to eight cylinders.

Across all three segments, the business model is identical: win a multi-year engineering design-in at the OEM drawing board, embed proprietary control firmware into the hardware, and ship millions of standardized, high-reliability control boxes over the life of the vehicle or generator platform.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The genius of SEDEMAC's combined ISG+EFI box is that it turns a regulatory cost (BS-VI fuel injection) and a consumer feature (silent start-stop) into a single BOM-saving architecture for the OEM. That is why adoption stuck—and why displacing SEDEMAC mid-platform is engineering-heavy.

book_subsections.title: Extending Sensorless Control Beyond Scooters: Power Tools, Voltage Regulators, and Export 3-Wheelers
paragraphs: If you stop at scooters and backup generators, you miss how horizontal SEDEMAC's core control stack really is. Any small rotating electric machine—whether it is a cordless drill, a saw, an electric three-wheeler, or a wet-magneto commuter motorcycle—faces the same physics problem: how do you know the rotor's exact position and speed without paying for fragile physical sensors? SEDEMAC has begun extending its sensorless commutation firmware into compact Motor Control Units for battery-powered power tools, smart FET-based single-phase and three-phase voltage regulators for two-wheelers, and Aftertreatment Control Modules (ACMs) for commercial emissions compliance.

On the November 2026 earnings call, management also laid out the next wave of commercial Mobility programs: full-scale ramp-ups of ISG ECUs for export three-wheelers, ISG ECU adoption on variant motorcycle models for top-tier domestic OEMs, and wet-magneto ISG kits targeted for commercial production in FY28. Each new socket reuses the same core firmware library while spreading R&D fixed costs over higher unit volumes. Still, you should keep the revenue math front and center: until those newer EV and export programs mature, ISG-led two-wheeler electronics remain the primary engine paying for all future optionality.
